## PDF page 11

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/GTO%20Crash%20Course%20Strategy%20Guide%20-%20Red%20Chip%20Poker.pdf#page=11)

```text
11 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE


  the question: “What would a properly-balanced strategy
  look like?”

  What particular strategy would my opponent not be well
  prepared for?

  Two approaches when your decision is unclear.
  Exploitative approach leads to guessing what you should
  do based on your assumptions about your opponents.
  Equilibrium approach means taking an action so that
  there is no “right” play for your opponent.

  Mixed Strategy – This concept means taking more
  than one action with the same hand or combo some
  percentage of the time. In the AKQ game, you might bet a
  King 33% of the time and check the King 67% of the time.
  The only time to deploy a mixed strategy is when you are
  indifferent between all of the options. If one option has a
  higher EV, you would not use a mixed strategy.

  Indifference – This concept refers to using a mixed
  strategy such that each action garners the same
  Expected Value.
```

  strategy really is.
  We often exploit the
  low-hanging fruit obvious to any thinking and studying
  player. Understanding GTO concepts will allow you
  to have a much more comprehensive understanding.
  Now that you understand what an equilibirum strategy
  is, you can see an exploitative strategy is a deviation
  from equlibrium, designed to profit from an opponent's
  deviation from equilibrium. Thus while it's easy to pick
  up on obvious deviations (mistakes) from our opponent,
  such as limping or overfolding, it's not that simple. Any
  exploitative strategy employed by you can be exploited
  by your opponent. If you are wrong about your opponent's
  mistake, or if they adjust to you, that deviation from
  equilibirum can quickly become unprofitable.

  The key is to know why exploitative strategies work
  and what they are designed to exploit. Most players
  employ highly exploitative/exploitable strategies without
  understanding what they are doing or why.

  quickly identify times when you need to stop using an
